title: Close config save safety findings
summary: Make backend settings save paths fail closed on canonical config contract violations, strict JSON confirmation drift, and core config-key ownership drift.
reason: Review found that settings save-patch could persist PSD1 config rejected by the canonical contract, string confirm_save values could pass backend truthiness checks, and core config code still imported config keys through a desktop compatibility shim.
behavior_before: Settings save validation could accept subtitle/OCR combinations later rejected by the canonical Config contract; confirm_save accepted truthy non-boolean values in backend handlers; core code depended on desktop config-key compatibility imports.
behavior_after: Settings save validation rejects canonical Config contract violations before write, mutation confirmation fields require literal JSON booleans, and core config-key imports use the backend-owned registry directly.
manual_validation: Focused unittest suite was attempted repeatedly. Individual settings-patch suite passed before concurrent source overwrites; later full focused suite failed because src/mediapipeline/core/config/settings_patch_candidate_facade.py and tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_settings_patch.py were overwritten during validation, reintroducing old unknown-key behavior.

RED baseline: bundled unittest service_config_validation currently fails expected subtitle contract cases; api_command_contracts fails expected strict boolean cases; application_facade_settings_patch fails expected unknown-key/OCR-save cases.
generate_config_schema --check - passed; refresh_summaries --changed - passed (3 written, 156 unchanged).
rollback_plan: Revert the config validation, command-contract, handler, import-cleanup, and test changes; refresh generated summaries; rerun the focused config/settings command-contract test set and settings smoke.
notes:
